scope.audience: A software developer comfortable with functions, objects, and ordinary application code, without assumed familiarity with each pattern catalog.

method: Structured source review across all articles; targeted follow-up on mechanisms, long implementations, terminology, example results, and responsive figures. This was not a line-by-line correctness verification of every implementation or a user study.

findings.title: Long incidental code lines require excessive sideways reading
findings.impact: The complete schema is harder to inspect than the record behavior it supports. On a phone, readers must pan repeatedly to understand a single declaration.
findings.recommendation: Wrap schema declarations and compound validation conditions at useful syntactic boundaries; retain native selectable code and horizontal scrolling.

findings.title: Show the short use-case trace before long implementations
findings.impact: Readers encounter lifecycle flags, validators, and transaction plumbing before seeing the small collaboration they are meant to recognize.
findings.recommendation: Lead the worked example with the application call and expected state transition, then identify the few implementation members to follow. Keep complete runnable files afterward.

findings.title: Lead Canary Release with the release decision, then explain fixture generation
findings.impact: A reader must retain several independent thresholds and positional rules before reaching the simple 3/25 stop decision.
findings.recommendation: Move the existing 0/10 then 3/25 trace before the code; put deterministic position rules and the separate quality gate after that overview.

findings.title: Give dense example outputs their field names at the point of comparison
findings.impact: Positional values, Python None, and Boolean flags make readers repeatedly consult the explanation to distinguish cancellation requested from actual cancellation.
findings.recommendation: Present the completion results as a small labeled table; print or display units and cache-miss names directly for Memoization.

findings.title: Explain the concrete action before specialized coordination terminology
findings.needle: A leader may lose coordination authority
findings.impact: Term, obsolete generation, fencing, and synchronous event demultiplexer arrive before an unfamiliar reader has an ordinary-language handle for the mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Define an increasing leadership-round number and destination-side stale-write rejection before naming fencing; introduce the selector as the wait-for-ready-resources facility before its formal role name.

findings.title: Expand incidental abbreviations where they first appear
findings.impact: Unexpanded DTO and ETL, plus owner-local revisions, add vocabulary work unrelated to understanding the API join or persistence mapping.
findings.recommendation: Use response records (data transfer objects, or DTOs), version numbers maintained by each service, and extract-transform-load (ETL) transformation at first use.

findings.title: Keep catalog maintenance history out of the central explanation
findings.impact: Canonical IDs, previous article titles, and search-alias bookkeeping interrupt the design explanation without helping a reader understand the pattern.
findings.recommendation: Retain useful established names in natural prose. Keep canonical IDs and collection-maintenance history in the existing authoring metadata.

findings.title: Name the object rather than its desktop position in alternative text
findings.impact: The alternative description says left order, while the phone illustration places Order A above Order B.
findings.recommendation: Replace left order with Order A in the article alt text and both SVG descriptions, preserving the explanation of separate mutable lists.

rendering.intersection_review: The single Sharding desktop footer flag is a bounding-box intersection. Visual review shows distinct, legible lines; it is not classified as an obscured-label defect.
rendering.scrolling_code_keyboard_focus: All overflowing code containers have tabindex=0.
rendering.manual_capture_review: Phone opening sheets for 12 articles; desktop overview sheet; selected code and full-size figures, including Active Record, Unit of Work, Sharding and Test Data Builder; Canary Release worked-example captures.

limitations: Editorial judgments target an assumed developer audience, not measured learning outcomes.
Long listings received targeted readability review; all examples were not rerun and no complete technical correctness audit is claimed.
All routes and responsive SVG variants were measured; manual visual review used representative captures rather than every image.
Phone checks use emulated browser viewports, not physical devices.
Embedded explorer controls and alternate states were not exercised.
The isolated preview is a content/source snapshot, not a new production build.

verification.suggested_sql_rewrite: Original and wrapped schemas produced matching accepted/rejected outcomes for eight boundary/null cases.
